sentence: The NHS says cutting down on saturated fat can help lower cholesterol, and that medicines such as statins are considered when lifestyle changes are not enough.
note: NHS: cut down on saturated fat; medicine if levels have not gone down after diet changes or high risk

sentence: High cholesterol means too much of a fatty substance called cholesterol in the blood, and it usually causes no symptoms.
note: High cholesterol too much fatty substance; usually causes no symptoms

sentence: The NHS advises cutting down on fatty food, especially saturated fat, and swapping to unsaturated fats.
note: Cut down on fatty food, especially saturated fat

sentence: Soluble fibre from foods such as oats, barley, beans and lentils is described as helping to lower cholesterol.
note: Soluble fibre helps lower cholesterol; oats, barley, beans, pulses, lentils

sentence: A blood test, sometimes called a lipid profile, measures cholesterol, and an NHS Health Check in England may offer it.
note: Blood test sometimes called lipid profile; NHS Health Check

sentence: High cholesterol means having too much of a fatty substance called cholesterol in the blood.
note: High cholesterol is when you have too much of a fatty substance called cholesterol in your blood

sentence: The body needs some cholesterol, but too much can narrow the arteries over time.
note: Your body needs some of it, but excess can narrow arteries over time

sentence: HDL is often called good cholesterol because it helps clear excess cholesterol from the blood, while LDL is the main type of bad cholesterol and can build up in artery walls.
note: HDL good; LDL main bad type

sentence: High cholesterol usually causes no symptoms, which is why a blood test is used to find it.
note: Usually no symptoms, so blood test important

sentence: Causes and risk factors listed by the NHS and the British Heart Foundation include eating a lot of fatty food, not being active enough, being overweight, smoking and drinking alcohol.
note: Fatty food, not exercising, overweight, smoking, drinking alcohol

sentence: It can also run in families, and the risk is higher for people over 50, men, people who have been through the menopause, and people of South Asian or sub-Saharan African origin.
note: Over 50, a man, menopause, South Asian or sub-Saharan African origin; runs in families

sentence: The NHS advises cutting down on fatty food, especially food containing saturated fat.
note: To reduce your cholesterol, try to cut down on fatty food, especially saturated fat

sentence: NHS and charity pages suggest unsaturated fats instead, such as oily fish, nuts, seeds and olive or rapeseed oil, and list butter, cream, hard cheese, cakes and biscuits among foods to limit.
note: Oily fish, nuts, seeds, olive or rapeseed oil; butter, cream, hard cheese, cakes, biscuits limited

sentence: Soluble fibre from oats, barley, beans, pulses and lentils is described as helping to lower cholesterol.
note: Soluble fibre helps lower cholesterol; oats, barley, beans, pulses, lentils

sentence: Plant sterols and stanols, added to some spreads and yoghurt drinks, can also help, although they are not suitable for everyone.
note: Plant sterols/stanols can help but one source warns not for some people

sentence: A hospital trust leaflet says cholesterol in foods such as eggs has little effect on blood cholesterol compared with saturated fat.
note: Eggs little effect compared with saturated fat (trust leaflet)

sentence: The NHS says medicine may be needed if cholesterol has not gone down after changes to diet and lifestyle, or if a person is at high risk of a heart attack or stroke.
note: You might need medicine if cholesterol has not gone down after changing diet and lifestyle, or at high risk of heart attack or stroke

sentence: Statins are the most common medicine for high cholesterol, and the NHS says people usually need to take them for life.
note: Statins most common medicine; usually take them for life

sentence: Testing is a blood test, sometimes called a lipid profile.
note: blood test, sometimes called a lipid profile

sentence: In England it can be offered as part of an NHS Health Check for people aged 40 to 74 who do not already have cardiovascular disease.
note: NHS Health Check if aged 40 to 74 and no cardiovascular disease

sentence: A GP may also suggest a test for someone with high blood pressure, diabetes, overweight, smoking or a family history of heart disease.
note: GP may suggest test if high blood pressure, diabetes, overweight, smoke, family history

sentence: Targets depend on age, other health conditions and heart risk, so the laboratory report and the clinician set what applies to each person.
note: Guidance on targets depends on age, other conditions, risk; ask your GP
